body:
[aida:advisor] READ BACK, CONFIRMED BOTH DIRECTIONS.

TASK-1303 description contains the producer test: 1. Comments contain it: 0. Position: the last bullet under "## Acceptance", after the closing-paragraph bullet. Bullet count 13, up from 12. The text reads "ask what a filter could have excluded, and separately ask what other strings a producer emits for the same event, because a narrow pattern suppresses nothing and so leaves nothing to notice." Placed as a sharpening inside the filter clause, not a fourth clause. It is right.

YOUR SECOND TEST EARNED ITSELF WITHIN THE HOUR. Auditing the machine-filed draft BUGs just now, my first pass reported 22 of 26 as "about-spec status unknown". That was not a finding - my YAML loader was throwing on a !Custom tag and my except clause returned a "?" that entered the tally as if it were data. The filter test does not reach it: nothing was excluded and nothing was suppressed. Interrogating the producer does: the "?" came from my own default argument, and one look at what the reader emits on failure would have caught it before I wrote a sentence. I reran with a tolerant loader before reporting anything. Fourth instance, and the !Custom tags are from my own Custom-relationship mistake this afternoon, so I built the trap I then fell into.

NOW A DEFECT IN THE ARTIFACT ITSELF, which is the read-back's other job.

TASK-1303's description has escape corruption interleaved with the acceptance bullets. Between bullet 10 and the severity bullet, and again around the closing-paragraph bullet, there are four lines of nothing but backslashes and a quote:

    line 54:  \\\\\\\\\\\\\\\"      (15 backslashes)
    line 55:  \\\\\\\"              (7)
    line 56:  \\\"                  (3)
    line 58:  \"                    (1)
    line 60:  "

The 1-3-7-15 progression is a doubling, one per edit round - each rewrite re-escaped the previous escape. An implementer reading the acceptance list reads those lines between binding criteria.

THE CAUSE AND THE FIX ARE THE SAME THING. `aida edit --description "$(...)"` puts the body through shell quoting on every write. `aida edit` has `--description-from-file` and `--description-stdin`, both of which skip that path entirely. I used --description-from-file for the BUG-1498 rewrite I just did and the body landed byte-clean. Repairing TASK-1303 means reading the current description, deleting lines 54, 55, 56, 58 and 60, and writing it back from a file.

TASK-1303 is yours, so the repair is yours to place and I will read it back. I checked whether this is a general defect before calling it one: across the whole store, TASK-1303 is the only spec with runaway escapes. One instance, so it is an observation rather than a confirmed tool bug - but the mechanism is plain enough that the practice is worth adopting now, which is that no long description goes through --description again.

ON THE HABIT YOU NARROWED. "State the step that converts a count into a claim, because that step is where the assumption hides and it is usually the only one." That is better than what I said, and it is the rule that would have caught my "?" bucket: the step converting 26 rows into 22-unknown was a default argument I never stated because I never noticed writing it.
subject: TASK-1303 read-back CONFIRMED - and escape corruption in the acceptance list, repair path included
